newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ economic activity falls in March qtr - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ economic activity falls in March qtr - SNZ.

text.p: Statistics New Zealand said on Monday the country's economic activity fell 0.5 percent in the March quarter, following a 0.7 percent rise in the December quarter.
Production is now 1.4 percent higher than in the March 1996 quarter.
SNZ said the quarterly fall was the first since the September 1992 quarter.
Annual growth is now at 2.3 percent for the March 1997 year, the lowest since the year ended June 1993, and well down on the growth rate of 6.7 percent for the June 1994 year.
SNZ said internal demand was quite flat in the March quarter, up by only 0.2 percent and now only 0.6 percent higher than a year ago.

After recovering slightly in the December quarter, household spending fell by 0.4 percent, with spending on durable goods down noticeably. It is now only 0.5 percent higher than for the March 1996 quarter.
"This fall in spending was countered by a 3.1 percent rise in investment, particularly for housing and other construction," SNZ said.
"The sluggish internal demand was further compounded by a weakening export sector, resulting in the 0.5 percent drop in quarterly GDP."
The level of activity in the service sector, including transport and retail, fell for the first time in 20 quarters, down 1.0 percent.
Manufacturing activity fell 1.1 percent in the quarter, a reversal of the rises recorded over the second half of last year. Annual growth for the year ended March 1997 was up 0.9 percent.

In spite of record levels of milk production, primary food production was down 3.5 percent in the quarter. This was due largely to meat production falling sharply after record growth in the December quarter.
A continuation of strong growth in dairy production resulted in a 0.6 percent rise in agricultural activity in the quarter, the second quarter of growth.
Investment in fixed assets, excluding residential buildings, rose 2.8 percent in the quarter and 4.5 percent in the March 1997 year.

Investment in new housing (which includes additions and alterations) rose for the second successive quarter, up 4.2 percent. It is now 6.3 percent higher than the same period a year ago. SNZ said it was possible some of the effect of last July's tax cuts went into improvements to housing rather than general consumer spending.
Exports fell 3.3 percent in the quarter, after rising throughout 1996. For the March year, total exports were up 4.6 percent.
After falling by 2.1 percent in the December quarter, import demand remained at similar levels, falling only 0.2 percent. For the March year, total imports were up 5.8 percent.
The expenditure-based measure of GDP fell 0.9 percent in the quarter, after a 0.6 percent rise in the December quarter.
SNZ said the GDP implicit price deflator, a broad measure of the overall price change for final goods and services produced in New Zealand, rose 1.8 percent in the March year.
